bibl.title: Demotic loans with mortgage in their legal-historical context. From the Ptolemaic period "Kaufpfandurkunde" to the Roman period bilingual loan with mortgage.
bibl.seg: Sandra Lippert, Demotic loans with mortgage in their legal-historical context. From the Ptolemaic period "Kaufpfandurkunde" to the Roman period bilingual loan with mortgage.

Sophie Démare-Lafont (ed.), Debt in Ancient Mediterranean Societies. A Documentary Approach. Legal Documents in Ancient Societies. VII. Paris, August 27-29, 2015 = École pratique des hautes études. Sciences historiques et philologiques. II. Hautes études orientales - Moyen et Proche-Orient. 8. 56 (Genève, 2019) pp. 123-152, figg.
bibl.note: Loans with mortgage appear in Egypt only in the Ptolemaic period. Almost from the beginning, two completely different concepts of how to establish a mortgage are present in the Demotic as well as in the Greek material: to draw up either one single document, a loan, which stipulates a property transfer of the mortgage object as a consequence of the non-repayment of the loan (Demotic "Kaufpfandurkunden", Greek "loan with mortgage") or two separate documents, a loan and a sale, with the sale not becoming effective unless the loan was not repaid (Greek loans accompanied by ὠναὶ ἐν πίστει; Fayumic Demotic/bilingual loans with mortgage). - Annexe: a. Ptolemaic period Demotic with mortgage [lists 12 documents]; - b. Roman period bilingual loans with mortgage [18 documents]; - c. Greek loans with mortgage [10 documents]; - d. Copies and abstracts [4 documents]; - e. Lender's renouncements for a mortgage after repayment of the loan [5 documents].
